name: explain
description: Ask the learner to EXPLAIN something in his own words — a graded check with NO options: he types a free-text answer. Unlike ask_user_question (no right answer), explain always has one. THE COMMITMENT RULE: correctAnswer is the FULL correct answer in your own words, reasoning included, COMMITTED before he ever sees the question. When his answer returns, grade it strictly against the commitment — never revise it after seeing his words. He sees the committed answer on submit. Set `nodeId` (required) to the plan node this question is about — validated at call time against the session's plan map. ONE question per turn: call a single explain, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

message.description: Your reply to him, shown as your normal message above the question: feedback on his last answer, the teaching or working that leads into it, anything he reads before answering. Write it here, not as text before the call: text before a tool call can be hidden from him.

type.description: REQUIRED — the question's role in the teaching cycle, as a bare word (no quotes): predict = posed BEFORE you teach the step (its own turn; the learner answers, then your teaching resolves it — arrives open, never collapsed); check = posed AFTER the step's teaching is complete (arrives collapsed behind the Check your understanding reveal). ONE question per turn either way.

nodeId.description: REQUIRED plan-tree node id this question is about — must EXACTLY match one of this session's plan_init node slugs (validated at call time; a mismatched id is rejected back to you). The lesson's position on the map derives from these tags (the node the latest tagged question is about is where the map stands; earlier ones count as visited). A node takes as many questions as it deserves: stay on one node for as many turns as the understanding needs — one reasoning step at a time, never rush forward. For off-map checks use ask_user_question.

question.description: The single question to ask. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next.

correctAnswer.description: REQUIRED. The full correct answer in your own words, reasoning included — COMMITTED before the learner ever sees the question. The commitment is immutable: when his answer returns, grade it strictly against this text — never revise the commitment after seeing his words, and never mark a wrong answer right to be kind. It is shown to him on submit; your next reply grades the nuance of what he wrote.

details.description: Optional, a line at most: HOW to answer — the format or shorthand you'll accept (e.g. "Shorthand is fine: '1 H/H – because…'"). Never teaching: cards, reference lists, definitions, recaps and explanations go in your reply's visible text, above the question.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the learner a single question and pause until they answer. NOT graded — there is no correct answer. Use when requirements are ambiguous, preferences are needed, a decision would materially affect the lesson, or you need an open-ended response. ONE question per turn: call a single ask_user_question, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

message.description: Your reply to him, shown as your normal message above the question: feedback on his last answer, the teaching or working that leads into it, anything he reads before answering. Write it here, not as text before the call: text before a tool call can be hidden from him.

nodeId.description: Optional plan-tree node id this question works on — an exercise or open question on that step. Must EXACTLY match one of this session's plan_init node slugs (validated at call time; a mismatched id, or one sent before there's a plan, is rejected back to you). Tag it so the map follows the lesson; leave it out for questions off the map (preferences, logistics).

question.description: The single question to ask the learner. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next question.

details.description: Optional, a line at most: HOW to answer — the format or shorthand you'll accept (e.g. "Shorthand is fine: '1 H/H – because…'"). Never teaching: cards, reference lists, definitions, recaps and explanations go in your reply's visible text, above the question.

label.description: Display label for the answer option — a bare claim, no reasoning

value.description: Optional machine-readable value returned for the option. Defaults to the label.

description.description: Optional extra detail shown below the option

options.description: Optional multiple-choice options. Omit for free-form text input. The learner can always choose 'Other' and type a custom answer when options are provided.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow multiple answers to the same question.

name: read
description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

name: ls
description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: the learner's home directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

name: find
description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Ignores node_modules, .git, and Library directories. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: the learner's home directory)

name: grep
description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Ignores node_modules, .git, and Library directories. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: the learner's home directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

name: plan_init
description: Write or REWRITE this session's plan map — the dependency graph the learner follows live in the plan window. Call once right after the probe concludes, to present the map; re-call whenever the map is wrong (the new block replaces the old tree). A mermaid graph block (any direction): one node per line (`slug[Short Title]` — slugs are permanent lowercase ids: a-z, 0-9, hyphens/underscores), `-->` edges meaning 'from must be understood before to' (chains fine). 5–15 nodes: a map, not a syllabus — one reasoning step per node, compress. Every check you fire names the node it assesses via `nodeId`; where the lesson stands derives from those tags.

mermaid.description:
A mermaid graph block (any direction), e.g.:
graph TD
  primitives[Number primitives] --> operators[Arithmetic operators] --> expressions[Evaluating expressions]
The only strict rule: ids are permanent lowercase slugs (a-z, 0-9, hyphens/underscores) — checks reference them via nodeId. Titles are free single-line text; `-->` means 'from = prerequisite' (chains fine); no subgraphs, styles, or classes.

name: research
description: Dispatch a background web-research agent: fact verification, current data, or niche specifics you are not certain about. The call is ASYNC and fire-and-forget — it resolves immediately and your turn continues; the research brief arrives later as a new message and the lesson resumes from it. Cite the brief's sources when you use them. NEVER use it for things you know cold, internal reasoning, or math.

question.description: The single research question to answer. Make it specific — the researcher sees nothing else of the lesson.

context.description: Why you need this / what the lesson needs it for — focuses the brief. One or two sentences.

name: demo
description: Dispatch a background sub-agent that BUILDS and headlessly TESTS an interactive teaching instrument — a single-file HTML demo (parameter sweep, simulation, animation, sampling) rendered live in the lesson. Use it when the concept is DYNAMIC: something to sweep, animate, or sample is better experienced than described. The call is ASYNC and fire-and-forget — it resolves immediately and your turn continues; the tested demo arrives later as a new message. Write a precise brief: concept, controls, interactions, style.

title.description: Short title for the demo card, e.g. 'Damped harmonic oscillator'.

brief.description: Precise brief for the builder: the concept, the parameters/controls and what each does, the interactions, and the visual style. The builder sees NOTHING else of the lesson — include everything it needs, including necessary formulas and constants.

name: visual
description: Dispatch a background sub-agent that hand-authors ONE precise SVG figure, renders it, LOOKS at the render, and iterates until correct. Use it for exact spatial pictures auto-layout diagrams can't do: coordinate geometry, number lines, vectors, function plots, physical layouts. For flows/relations/taxonomies write mermaid inline instead. The call is ASYNC and fire-and-forget — it resolves immediately and your turn continues; the verified figure arrives later as a new message.

brief.description: Precise brief for ONE static figure: exactly what it must show — coordinates, labels, proportions, orientation. The maker sees NOTHING else of the lesson; a wrong or vague brief produces a wrong figure.

name: pdf
description: Dispatch a background sub-agent that READS a learner-provided PDF on your behalf (triage, targeted extraction, visual page reading for equations and diagrams) and returns a brief with page citations. Use it when the learner gives you a PDF path and you need its CONTENT for the lesson. The call is ASYNC and fire-and-forget — it resolves immediately and your turn continues; the brief arrives later as a new message. For quick looks at plain text or image files, use the read tool directly instead of dispatching.

path.description: Path to the learner's PDF (relative or absolute), exactly as they gave it.

question.description: What you need from the document — the specific content, explanation, or answer to extract and brief. The reader sees NOTHING else of the lesson.
